constituents.title: Saved 'No' ignored once the time zone leaves Europe
constituents.section: 2. The privacy choice
constituents.why_it_matters: Suppose a visitor answers 'No, send nothing' while their browser is set to a European time zone. On their next visit from a time zone outside Europe, they are counted and reported anyway. The reason: `allowed()`, the one rule both tools follow, is defined as section 2's table. Its 'Outside Europe' row allows everything, whatever answer is saved, and the 15 unit-test cells lock that in. This contradicts the Goal's 'one answer governs' and G3's 'by default'. It also breaks the 'Extending later' plan for NH-349, the 'Privacy choices' link for every visitor: if a visitor outside Europe says 'No' through that link, the next page load overrides it. Letting a saved answer win for every visitor, with the time zone deciding only whether to ask when nothing is saved, fixes both for the cost of one table row.

findings.title: No privacy notice: the popup never says who runs the site or that an answer can be withdrawn

constituents.title: No privacy notice: consent lacks controller and withdrawal right
constituents.section: 3. The popup — the approved words (with G9, the home-page disclosure)
constituents.why_it_matters: A 'Yes' given in Europe may not be valid consent, and valid consent is the outcome G3 and G5 ('whatever is good by law') exist to secure. The EDPB's consent guidelines (05/2020) and the CNIL's cookie guidelines count consent as informed only when the visitor is told at least who is asking, each purpose, the data used, and that they can withdraw. The approved words name the purposes and tools but not who runs the site or the right to withdraw, and the site has no privacy page to hold that information; Google Analytics' terms (section 7) also require 'an appropriate Privacy Policy', not only the disclosure link G9 relies on. The words are leocaseiro's, and which name and contact to publish is leocaseiro's decision.

findings.title: The end-to-end tests would reach Google, and the source of Google's script in tests is undecided

constituents.title: Every existing lane test would still reach Google
constituents.section: 9. Testing (End to end, Playwright) and 1. Packages and files
constituents.why_it_matters: Every existing test in the `web` lane would download Google's gtag.js and send page-view hits to Google on every CI and local run. The fake Google Analytics ID and the Sydney time zone apply to the whole one-build lane, but only `privacy-choice.e2e.ts` installs the fixture that answers Google's hosts. `player.e2e.ts`, `a11y.e2e.ts`, `toast-occlusion.e2e.ts` and `pages.vr.ts` import `test` straight from `@playwright/test`, and none of them is on the changed-files list. Sentry's opt-in fixture is safe only because its fake DSN host is `.invalid` and never resolves. `www.googletagmanager.com` does resolve, and the spike showed that a made-up ID still gets a working script that sends a page view. A module-scope call that every lane file makes, the same shape `failOnUnexpectedPageErrors()` already has, keeps 'no test reaches Google' true and keeps a live third-party host out of the merge-blocking lane.
constituents.suggested_fix: Have web/e2e/google-analytics.ts export a module-scope call, the same shape as failOnUnexpectedPageErrors(), that answers Google's hosts for every test in the calling file. Add web/e2e/player.e2e.ts, a11y.e2e.ts, toast-occlusion.e2e.ts and pages.vr.ts to 'Changed files' as callers of it. State in section 9 that every test in the lane answers Google's hosts locally, not only privacy-choice.e2e.ts.

constituents.why_it_matters: About a hundred existing cases (player, accessibility, toast and the ten screenshots) will download Google's script and send real hits to Google from CI, which contradicts 'no test reaches Google'. The lane's one build gets the fake Google Analytics ID and every project runs as Sydney, so startAnalytics() runs on each page load. Only cases that install the new fixture get local answers, and the four existing files import test directly from @playwright/test. Sentry's fake DSN never had this gap because it is on .invalid, which cannot resolve, while Google's hosts do resolve; the spec also does not say where the fixture gets the real gtag.js that the gcs, npa and dt assertions need, and the spike answered only Google's collect requests locally.

The fixture fetches the real gtag.js with route.fetch(), which runs in Node and so is not affected by that rule, and answers every hit locally. Change section 9's claim to 'no test sends Google a hit'.

constituents.title: E2E assertions need Google's real gtag.js; its source is undecided
constituents.section: 9. Testing (End to end, Playwright)
constituents.why_it_matters: The Sydney, 'Yes' and privacy cases check `gcs=G101`, `npa=1` and `dt`. Only Google's own gtag.js puts those values on its collect requests. Yet section 9 answers every Google host locally and never says what the fixture returns for the script itself. If the fixture serves a stub script, the page sends no collect request at all: the Sydney case cannot pass, and the privacy case ('no Google request contains the title') passes while checking nothing. leocaseiro needs to choose between two options. (1) Commit a snapshot of the gtag.js that Google serves for the fake ID as a test fixture: no test reaches Google, but a Google-owned script then sits in a public repository, and the tests run a frozen copy until someone refreshes it. (2) Let only the script download through to Google, as the spike did: the tests run the live script, but the merge-blocking `web` job then depends on googletagmanager.com, and section 9's promise becomes 'no hit reaches Google'. Whichever is chosen, the privacy case should also check that at least one collect request was recorded.

findings.synthesis_note: Merged: one strategy resolves all three. Feasibility#1 (anchor 100) and adversarial#4 describe the same leak (existing test files never install the fixture; Google's hosts resolve, unlike Sentry's .invalid DSN) with different mechanisms (a call in every file, versus a fail-closed resolver rule in the config). Feasibility#2 adds that the gcs/npa/dt assertions need Google's real gtag.js and nothing says where the fixture gets it (snapshot committed, or live). Choosing the script source is a real trade-off (Google-owned code in a public repo, versus a merge-blocking lane that depends on googletagmanager.com), so the merged finding is a decision. The case also never presses a control whose label holds a track name, such as Solo and Mute, which TrackRow labels with the track's name; that is the leak path G8 cites. findings.title: The accessibility scan asks for a dark theme web/ cannot show

constituents.title: Dark-theme axe scan targets a state web/ cannot reach
constituents.section: 9. Testing - Screenshots and accessibility (axe scan), and 3. The popup - Themes
constituents.why_it_matters: An implementer following section 9 has to inject a .dark class from the test to scan a theme no visitor can reach: web/app/layout.tsx renders a bare html element with no theme control, and every existing web axe case is light-only. The repo's web visual-regression spec (docs/specs/2026-09-21-web-visual-regression-gate.md, 'Light only') rules this out, calling dark mode unreachable in web/ and a test-injected .dark 'test-only instrumentation of exactly the kind this project bans'. The dark scan would also audit the rest of /play in a theme nobody has audited, so unrelated findings could land on this ticket. Scanning in light only matches the other axe cases and removes the problem.
constituents.suggested_fix: In section 9, change the accessibility bullet to: 'An axe scan with the popup open, in the light theme like the rest of the web lane.' In section 3, change the Themes bullet to: 'Themes: colours come from the design tokens; no new colour.'

constituents.title: 'Both themes' axe scan is unreachable in light-only web/
constituents.section: 9. Testing — Screenshots and accessibility, last bullet (line 398); 3. The popup — Themes bullet (line 164)
constituents.why_it_matters: The test plan asks for a step the `web` lane cannot perform: `web/` can never show dark mode, because the variant is the class `.dark` (`client/src/styles.css:27`), nothing sets it, and `web/app/layout.tsx` renders a bare `<html lang="en">`. findings.title: Typed fields stop object literals only; track() forwards whatever object it is given

constituents.title: Typed fields catch literals only; track() forwards everything
constituents.section: 5. Events
constituents.why_it_matters: The promise that 'text from the file cannot reach Google' only holds where a call passes an object literal. TypeScript skips its excess-property check for an object that is built first, or merged in with a spread. So a fields object that also carries a track name still type-checks, and `track()` forwards the whole object to `gtag('event', …)`. If `track()` copies only the keys declared for that event, the promise holds for every call shape, for the cost of one key list per event. The privacy e2e case cannot catch this, because it covers opening a file, not every control.
constituents.suggested_fix: In section 5, track() sends only the fields declared for that event. They are read from a per-event key list kept beside AnalyticsEvents, with the types derived from it; the fields object is never forwarded as given.

findings.title: Click IDs such as fbclid in the page address reach Google

constituents.why_it_matters: A visitor who arrives from a Facebook link brings an `fbclid` (Meta's identifier for that click) in the `?` part. residual_concerns.text: 'Extending later' tells NH-349 that 'a consent update to denied' stops Google Analytics. Google's consent-mode help page says a loaded tag with analytics_storage denied keeps sending cookieless pings, which are the pings G3 rejected as needing consent. NH-349 (out of scope here) will therefore need to stop the tag, not only update consent.

deferred_questions.text: Where does `<PrivacyChoices />` sit in the DOM and the tab order? Section 1 says only that `layout.tsx` renders it. Rendered first, a keyboard user meets the question at once but passes four extra Tab stops (three answers and Details) on every page until answering; rendered last, as the Toaster is, it comes after a dozen or more page controls (the a11y lane's floor for `/play` is 12), which is why `Sonner.tsx` gave the Toaster an Alt+T hotkey. The plan must pick one and add an e2e assertion for the choice.

restated_suppressed.text: What does the Google fixture in web/e2e/google-analytics.ts serve for the gtag.js script, and is it installed for every Playwright test? Section 1 (Packages and files) puts a fake Google Analytics ID in the whole lane's config and defaults every project to Sydney, so Google Analytics starts in every end-to-end test and in all ten existing screenshots; section 9 (Testing) says the fixture answers Google's hosts so no test reaches Google, yet the Sydney assertions on gcs=G101 and npa=1 need Google's own script, which the spike let load from googletagmanager.com while answering only the collect requests locally. The plan must either pin a copy of the script and install the routing for all tests, or narrow the claim to collect requests.

When a visitor's saved answer is 'Report errors only' or 'No, send nothing' and their time zone later reads as outside Europe, does the saved answer still govern? Section 2 (The privacy choice) gives 'Outside Europe' everything and has no row for a stored refusal, allowed() is specified as exactly that table, and the 15-cell unit test in section 9 would not cover the case either way, so the plan has to choose between honouring the stored refusal and following the time zone.
